SMTO-API-0008 — SMTO couldn't find what you asked for

GUID: 4baaf4ca-5e2f-46a6-95e9-e6ab3de4b27e
Slug: api-resource-not-found
Domain: API · Subsystem: api

What happened

  • The item or page you tried to open isn't there. It may have been deleted or cleaned up automatically, the link may be old, or this page may be out of date.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Reload the page, then open the item again from its list, such as the conversation list, instead of using an old link or bookmark. A saved link can point to something that was renamed, moved or deleted since you saved it.
  2. If a page looks broken or half loaded after SMTO was updated, reload it fully with Ctrl+Shift+R (Cmd+Shift+R on a Mac). An old copy of the page can ask for files the updated SMTO no longer has.
  3. If a conversation has disappeared, check whether Auto-purge is turned on in Settings › Data. Auto-purge permanently deletes unpinned conversations after a period without new work, and deleted items can't be opened.

What success looks like

  • The item or page opens normally.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the link you used, to the person who manages SMTO. Don't keep using an old link after someone else changed the item; open it fresh from its list.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • An SMTO resource or static-asset lookup found no matching item for the requested identifier or path (including static files outside the console allowlist or site fingerprint map), or an otherwise unclassified HTTP 404 was returned.

What this means

  • Resource/static lookup cannot locate an allowed requested item, or the generic HTTP boundary maps an otherwise unclassified 404. Generic API status and exception families establish only their stated boundary. Stronger structured causes take precedence; the original receipt determines whether work started or had effects, and diagnostics add no dispatch or retry.

Why this can happen

  • Resource/static lookup cannot locate an allowed requested item, or the generic HTTP boundary maps an otherwise unclassified 404.

How to diagnose it

  • Verify the route and current resource identity; absence in this scope does not prove global deletion.

How to fix it

  • Check the endpoint and identifier in Technical details against the current list endpoint; the resource may have been deleted, purged or belong to another scope. For static assets, confirm the requested file is in the console allowlist or the site fingerprint map and reload clients that hold stale asset URLs.
  • Refresh the current resource list and use an existing identifier in the owning scope.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • A current authorized resource reference resolves through its owning route.

What not to do

  • Do not submit a stale identifier or revision after another actor changed the resource.

Technical notes

  • Generic API status and exception families establish only their stated boundary. Stronger structured causes take precedence; the original receipt determines whether work started or had effects, and diagnostics add no dispatch or retry.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
